title: Zesty Venezuelan Corn Tagine
description: A tangy, bouncy, low-sodium Venezuelan tagine that pairs sweet corn with buttermilk and a citrus vinaigrette, finished with a spherified splash of lime for a festive pop.
instructions: Rinse 4 cups of fresh corn kernels and pat dry.
Heat a tagine pot over medium heat and swirl a tablespoon of olive oil around the base.
Add 1 chopped onion and 2 minced garlic cloves, sauté until translucent.
Stir in 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and a pinch of cayenne, cooking for 30 seconds.
Pour in 2 cups of buttermilk, 1 cup of diced tomatoes, and the corn, stirring to combine.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the corn simmers, whisk 200 milliliters lime juice with 0.5 gram sodium alginate and let sit for 30 minutes.
Prepare a calcium chloride bath by dissolving 1 gram in 200 milliliters water.
Drop the lime alginate mixture into the calcium bath using a spoon, letting spheres form for 1 minute before transferring to a bowl of cold water.
When the corn is tender, stir in 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, 1 teaspoon sea salt, and the spherified lime spheres.
Adjust seasoning with lemon zest and a drizzle of olive oil, then remove from heat.
Serve hot, garnished with extra cilantro and lime wedges.
